title: harness-config
description: The set of keys the harness reads out of a target repository's .harness/config.yaml. The declared properties are the whole of that set: a key a target's config file carries and no harness code reads is out of the set by construction. This file is checked against a target's config at pre-flight: a key it does not declare refuses the run, naming the offending key and this declared set, so a mistyped key stops rather than silently taking a default. It is a contract rather than an artifact shape, so no stage is asked to produce or satisfy it; what holds it is coverage, asserted as set equality against declared_config_keys() in both directions. Every declared key carries a proof that varies it to a value the harness would never pick and observes the harness obey it. Types are the types harness_config.load_config produces: every scalar is a string, because the config parser never coerces, and a list-valued key is an array of strings.

allowed_tools.description: Bash command patterns stage agents may run without prompting. Passed to every agent invocation as --allowedTools, and injected into the shared harness-layer prompt partial as {{allowed_tools}}.

architecture_docs.description: Repository-relative paths of the architecture documents assembled into every stage's context.

base_branch.description: The branch a story branch is cut from and the branch l5-plan expects to commit a plan artifact onto. Unset, the base is resolved from refs/remotes/origin/HEAD and then from the literal main.

branch_prefix.description: Prepended to a story id to form the story branch name. Defaults to story/.

census_command.description: The command a stage declaring suite_census has run in a clone at its baseline and again in the tree it left. It must print to stdout a JSON object of counter names to integers. The target supplies it, chooses the counters, and phrases them so that a larger number is a stronger suite; the coordinator parses the object and interprets no name, which is what keeps the harness free of any knowledge of the target's test framework. Its absence disables the census: the check is recorded as one that did not run rather than as a pass, and nothing is announced, because nothing is about to take a census's worth of time.

history_dir.description: Directory, relative to the target root, holding the harness-scoped cross-run history: the append-only logs schemas/cross-run-history.schema.json declares. Defaults to .harness/history. Unlike runs_dir and logs_dir it is versioned, because the records are what outlive the run directories they describe, and it is a blocked path for every stage, because a stage must not be able to edit the record of its own execution.

history_retention_days.description: How long a cross-run history record is kept, in days. A string like every other configured scalar, because the config parser coerces nothing; it is parsed to a non-negative number and a value that is not one refuses the run. Unset, nothing is ever pruned and the whole history is kept, so pruning is opt-in. Set, records whose timestamp is older than the bound are dropped from each log by the prune that runs once per run, at run-directory creation and before that run's first append — which is the only point at which a log is rewritten, and it announces itself. A record whose timestamp cannot be read is kept rather than dropped: this store never discards what it cannot judge. It is a retention bound and not a calibration window; a reader that needs recent samples expresses one as a query bound over a log that was never pruned on its behalf.

logs_dir.description: Directory, relative to the target root, holding raw agent output logs. Defaults to .harness/logs.

mandate_max_depth.description: How many links the resolution of a story's mandate may follow before it gives up, as a count of hops. A string like every other configured scalar, because the config parser coerces nothing; it is parsed to a non-negative integer and a value that is not one is not obeyed. Unset, the bound is 8. A bound exists at all because a chain that cannot terminate must be refused rather than followed: a walk that has not reached a human within it is refused naming this bound, which is a different refusal from one that found no link to follow and from one that came back to somewhere it had already been. Raising it does not make an unresolvable chain resolvable; it only decides how long the harness spends discovering that.

max_pause_wait_seconds.description: How long a run paused on capacity exhaustion may wait in place before the process exits, in seconds. A ceiling on a wait whose length the harness has been told, never a duration it sleeps in the absence of one: a capacity signal carrying a reset time within this bound is slept to and the stage re-entered, one carrying a reset time beyond it exits, and one carrying no reset time at all exits without sleeping. A string like every other configured scalar, because the config parser coerces nothing; it is parsed to a non-negative number and a value that is not one refuses the run at pre-flight, naming the key and the value. Unset, it is zero — never wait, always exit paused — so the only duration written in harness source is the one that means do not wait, and every wait the harness takes comes from here.

model.description: The Claude model each stage invocation is run with. Unset, the agent runner passes no model and the developer's default is used.

permission_mode.description: The permission mode each stage invocation is run under. Defaults to acceptEdits.

runs_dir.description: Directory, relative to the target root, holding per-run state, events and artifacts. Defaults to .harness/runs. Also what l5-status lists.

standards_dir.description: Directory, relative to the target root, holding the repository standards injected into every stage's context. Defaults to .harness/standards.

stories_dir.description: Directory, relative to the target root, holding approved story artifacts. Defaults to .harness/stories. Also the directory l5-plan snapshots to decide what a planning session produced.

sweep_max_entries.description: How many pending entries one sweep of the outbox may attempt to file. It bounds filing attempts and not entries read: a landed, failed or poisoned entry reaches no transport, so a queue holding them is fully reported however small this is, and only pending entries are ever left over. Entries past the bound are left pending and unattempted, and the sweep's summary names the bound and how many it left undone rather than truncating silently. The worst case of one sweep is therefore this multiplied by sync_timeout_seconds, so a reader raising one should consider the other: the opportunistic sweeps sit in front of a run and after its completion commit, where that product is time a developer waits. A string like every other configured scalar, because the config parser coerces nothing. l5-sync refuses a value that is not a positive integer, naming the key and the value, because a terminal invocation a developer asked for should not quietly obey a bound it cannot read; an opportunistic sweep notes it and files nothing, because a sweep that could refuse would make an unreadable bound stop a run. Unset, it is 20.

sync_command.description: The command the outbox files an entry by running. The harness invokes it once per entry and knows nothing else about the tracker: the entry goes to it on stdin as a JSON document carrying the key, the identity, the state and the payload; the entry's key is also in its environment as L5_SYNC_KEY, taken from the same field as the copy on stdin so the two cannot disagree; and the exit code is the whole of the answer. Zero lands the entry and the reference is the last non-empty line of stdout — recorded and never parsed, so a reference that is not a URL lands exactly as one that is. 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL) leaves the entry pending with the attempt counted, so a later sync tries again. Every other non-zero code fails the entry terminally and no later sync invokes the command for it. What the command said on stderr is carried back as the entry's last_error, bounded to a tail. The command must be idempotent given the key: it is expected to search the tracker for that key before it creates anything, which is what makes the ambiguous write — created, response lost — safe to retry, and the harness cannot enforce it. A sync command must not commit: it writes, and a human or a run commits; the harness does not enforce that either and says so rather than implying a check that does not exist. templates/sync/github.sh is a reference implementation of the whole contract. Unset, no transport is built, l5-sync reports the queue as it stands and files nothing.

sync_timeout_seconds.description: How long a sync command may run before it is killed, in seconds. A string like every other configured scalar, because the config parser coerces nothing; l5-sync parses it to a positive number and refuses, naming the key and the value, when it is not one. Unset, it is 60 seconds rather than zero: a timeout of zero here would be no timeout at all, which is the failure the bound exists to prevent, so the default duration written in harness source is a real one and every path through the transport is bounded in time. The kill reaches the command's process group rather than the command alone — the command is spawned in its own session — so a command that spawned children of its own leaves none of them behind. A command killed this way leaves its entry pending rather than failed, because a command that ran past its timeout established nothing about whether the request arrived.

tests_dir.description: Where a target's tests live, as a repository-relative path prefix ending in a slash. Set, it is the prefix the workflow's {{tests_dir}} token resolves to, so the stage restricted from creating tests is restricted there and the stage that writes them is told to write them there. There is no default: unset, the target declares no test directory at all, the token resolves out of the list it appears in entirely rather than becoming an empty prefix that would match every path, and the restriction does not exist for that target.

test_command.description: The command the clean-clone and revert checks run inside a scratch clone. Read without a fallback: a target that omits it cannot run either check.

test_selection_command.description: The command the revert check substitutes a nominated test into, run in a clone and read for its exit status alone. The substitution point is the literal {test}, replaced by the string the writing stage nominated; every other character of the command is the target's own, and the harness knows nothing about the selector syntax it is substituting into. Set, it lets the revert check short-circuit: the nomination is run once in a clone with the stage's edits applied, where it must pass, and once in the clone with the governed edits reverted, where it must fail, and pass-then-fail permits the edits without the configured test_command being run at all. Unset, the short-circuit is disabled and the check reaches today's verdict by today's path — the whole configured test command in the reverted clone. Its absence disables the short-circuit; it never fails the check, and it is never read as a permission.

verification_runner.description: The executable the clean-clone and revert checks run the configured test command under: it replaces the first word of test_command, and every remaining argument is the configured command's own. Unset, the checks use test_command's own first word, so the command runs exactly as written. An environment difference that cannot be expressed as a first-word swap belongs in test_command instead.

workflow.description: The name of the workflow definition under workflows/ that a run executes. Defaults to story-workflow.
